summary.headline: Sutlej Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (6.7% margin) from INR5 crore, with PBT of INR4.2 crore versus a loss a year ago.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose 17% YoY to INR704 crore, marginally ahead of Q4 FY26. Gross margin expanded about 370 bps to 46.8%, with raw material cost falling to 53.2% of revenue from 56.9%. EBITDA margin has now expanded for five consecutive quarters (0.8%, 2.7%, 3.9%, 5.3%, 6.7%). Management said the quarter was clean with no exceptional items and that all three business clusters and six manufacturing units delivered positive EBITDA. Value-added yarn share is still only about 10-15% against a 30-35% target.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR640 crore, up 16% YoY; segment EBITDA INR34.4 crore vs INR6.5 crore a year ago. Management attributes about 60% of the 2.5% raw-material-to-sales improvement to moving up product categories and the balance to operational efficiency.

segments.name: Sutlej Green Fibre (recycled PET)
segments.commentary: Gross sales roughly INR400 crore; about 70-75% is consumed internally by the group's own units. Management is adding performance properties to recycled polyester and discussing collaborations with brands.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Revenue up 22% YoY and profitability held versus a loss a year ago. Sequentially softer on order phasing, not demand. Management targets doubling the business in about two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal quarterly guidance. Management said it will maintain or better Q1 numbers in Q2 and Q3, but declined to give a clear outlook.
Long-term aim is a double-digit EBITDA margin, described as the near-term benchmark; no timeline was given.
Finance cost in absolute terms expected to rise to about INR75 crore this year from about INR67 crore last year, due to capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.
Rationalization programme is not complete; remaining cost benefits expected through the balance of FY27.
Employee cost expected to decline in coming quarters, per management, with no quantified target.
Southeast Asia and Latin America market entries are expected this financial year.
Technical textiles (Protech) and protective textiles are expected to contribute in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex is mainly upgrading existing assets rather than new capacity; funded from internal accruals and existing facilities with no additional equity, per management.
Maintenance capex is proceeding as planned.
Protech technical textiles has moved from qualification into sampling and trials; some protective textile products have qualified.
Home textile growth plans are underway, with the business in investment mode for technical and protective textiles.
demand_pricing: Global demand described as relatively stable; management said legacy yarn makers benefited from China-driven demand in cotton-grade yarn, which Sutlej does not directly target.

Export markets: Far East and Africa, opened last year, have moved from trial volumes to repeat orders. Core markets Latin America and Europe are steady; Bangladesh demand is stable but below levels of two years ago. Exports go to about 60 destinations.
Customers are rebuilding inventories cautiously from very low levels.

Raw material outlook: cotton expected flat to slightly higher, with parity emerging between international and Indian prices; polyester/synthetics expected to ease over the long term, but a return to pre-war levels is uncertain.
Cotton is about 30% of fibre consumption by quantity; synthetics about 70%, of which about 30% of the total is recycled.
Value-added yarn is about 10-15% of yarn products against a 30-35% target. Customer trials take 3-6 months, and first containers of new specialty SKUs have shipped for testing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn portfolio is value-added now, and what EBITDA margin can the business reach at 30-35% value-added?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is about 10-15% of yarn products, with a pipeline and new SKUs under customer evaluation. Management would not give a margin number for the steady state but said double-digit EBITDA is the minimum target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the yarn EBITDA gain came from spread expansion versus mix and integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of the raw material-to-sales improvement (about 2.5 percentage points) came from moving up product categories; the rest came from operational efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost (15-17% of revenue) so far above peers, and will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ratio is not at target and will fall in coming quarters. It attributed the gap to melange and dyeing layers, job processing in home textiles, and low realisations, and said absolute costs have not risen.

qa_highlights.question: What will the interest outflow be this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost is expected to rise to about INR75 crore from about INR67 crore last year, because of capex, even though the cost-of-borrowing percentage is down about 40 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and EBITDA potential of Green Fibre and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Green Fibre gross sales are about INR400 crore, of which 70-75% is consumed internally. Home textiles are to be doubled in about two years, with no margin target given.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt be structured, and how do raw material prices affect working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital borrowing will rise for the same number of days because of higher raw material prices. Long-term debt is mainly for capex, which is secured. Credit lines will be rebalanced as results move.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Q2 and Q3 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance. Management said it will try to maintain or better the Q1 numbers.

risks_watch: Sustainability of margin: management attributes ~60% of the ~2.5pp raw-material-to-sales improvement to moving up product categories; track whether yarn EBITDA holds once polyviscose spreads normalise.
Value-added yarn share is only ~10-15% vs 30-35% target; new specialty SKUs still in 3-6 month customer trials, so watch for repeat orders.
Employee cost at 15-17% of revenue remains well above peers per analyst pushback; management gave no quantified target and said reduction will come over the next few quarters.
Finance cost guided up to ~INR75 crore from ~INR67 crore due to capex and higher working-capital borrowing from raw material prices; watch PBT absorption as margins scale.
Cotton expected flat to slightly higher and synthetics expected to ease only over the long term, so raw-material input-cost direction remains uncertain.
Protech technical textiles and protective textiles expected to contribute only from FY28; no near-term contribution from these new businesses in FY27.
key_quotes: This result was not produced by a market turn, a commodity tailwind or a onetime gain.
We are not declaring a turnaround complete and the burden of proof rests with us.
So, I will refrain from wanting to give you a very clear number.
And I did not give a horizon as to where -- when we will get into two digits.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's quality and on execution against the stated plan, but explicitly cautious on forward numbers: management declined to give a Q2/Q3 outlook, a steady-state margin figure, or a timeline for double-digit EBITDA. It was defensive and vague when pressed on employee cost and value-added mix, attributing gaps to the business model and "journey" framing.
